data.narrative:
Rivan is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Harvey Hodd that has raised $47.2M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 9 peers in the Climate & Energy sector—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix—though same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables proved insufficient for reliable peer-median analysis.

Given data constraints, the valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage advancement to the $47M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $94M. This single-method anchor generates a triangulated range of $80M (low-end scenario) to $109M (high-end scenario), with $94M as the median point.

The analysis is constrained by the absence of sufficiently granular same-stage or adjacent-stage peer multiples in the Climate & Energy sector. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peer cohorts, path-to-profitability, and technology de-risking milestones. Any valuation within the $80M–$109M band should be stress-tested against Series B market conditions and sector-specific capital requirements before deployment in term-sheet negotiation.
